item.title: "Dublin city centre lacking what other European cities offer" - Cavan native
item.description: A Co Cavan man believes Dublin's O'Connell Street is lacking what other European city centres have. Kilnaleck native Darren Gaffney posed the question on social media asking what has the main thoroughfare in Dublin to offer. He says when you think of other European cities, the centres are bustling and full of high standard retail outlets. item.title: Calls by Cavan councillor to scrap planned €50 charge for blister packs
item.description: A local councillor has called on the Minister for Health to reverse the decision of the €50 charge for blister packs. A decision by the Government to withdraw funding from this month for blister packs issued by pharmacies have been delayed following political backlash to the decision. Cllr Damien Brady wants to see the idea of charging for the medication holders scraped altogether. item.title: Break-in to local community led cafe strongly condemned
item.description: A break-in to a local community led cafe has been strongly condemned. Gardai are investigating a break which occurred on Saturday night in Carrickroe. The community led Coffee Doc, The Village Brew was broken into after 1am. Carrickroe Community Development confirmed that Gardai have examined the CCTV footage from the local coffee shop. item.title: Monaghan woman on her time in Australian mines
item.description: A Monaghan native, who has been living in Australia for many years, has opened up about her experience working in the mines there. Arlene Dooley, who is from Inniskeen, left Monaghan and began working in the Australian mines 13 years ago. Arlene said the mines were not a part of her plan when she left Ireland, but she said that the industry has offered her a lot. item.title: Funding needed for salting roads in Ballybay/Clones
item.description: Members of the Ballybay-Clones Municipal District are calling for additional funding and resources to support the salting and gritting of rural roads. Following today's meeting, it was unanimously agreed that the MD would now write to the Department of Transport and to Darragh O'Brien, Minister for Transport.
